items.title: From Okhla to Badarpur: 5 Delhi seats that lost over 40% of their 2025 electorate
items.summary: The draft roll as part of the Special Intensive Revision exercise is out for Delhi. Of 1,45,10,299 electors, 47,56,722 are currently out – nearly one in every three persons excluded. Seven of Delhi’s 70 constituencies recorded more than 1 lakh deletions each. In descending order in terms of sheer numbers, these are Burari, Okhla, Badarpur, Vikaspuri, Matiala, Rithala, and Karawal Nagar. In terms of deletions compared to the size of the electorate, five constituencies had more than 40 percent of their 2025 electorate missing from the draft roll. These were Tughlakabad, Okhla, R.K. Puram, Jangpura and Badarpur. Of these five, three were won by the AAP and two by the BJP in the 2025 Delhi assembly election. Five seats with the highest deletion rates as per the draft roll. Tughlakabad saw the highest deletion rate. Of the 2,04,867 electors registered during the 2025 election, 92,033 are missing from the draft roll – nearly one in two voters. Though these numbers are not final as the final list will only be published on November 4 – after the claims and objections round concludes on September 30 and the notice period finishes on October 29. items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice AY Kogje as Chief Justice of Madhya Pradesh High Court
items.summary: Justice Alpesh Yeshvant Kogje from Gujarat High Court has been recommended for appointment as the Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The recommendation was made by the Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on August 31. Justice Kogje is presently serving as a judge of the Gujarat High Court. Justice Kogje completed his B.Sc. in Chemistry in 1990 and earned his law degree from the Faculty of Law at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda in 1993. He joined the Bar in 1993, building a robust practice in civil and criminal matters before the High Court. Throughout his career as counsel, he held several significant roles, including Additional Public Prosecutor from 2002 to 2007, Standing Counsel for the Central Excise and Customs Department, and Special Public Prosecutor for the Special Investigation Team (SIT), where he notably handled a large volume of important cases arising from the 2002 Godhra riots. He was elevated as an Additional Judge of the Gujarat High Court in April 2016. He was subsequently appointed as a permanent Judge of the Gujarat High Court in March 2018. items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Jammu & Kashmir High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Justice Bhati is currently a judge of the Rajasthan High Court. The decision to recommend his name for Chief Justice was taken by the collegium in a meeting held on August 31. If the Centre confirms the collegium's recommendation, Justice Bhati will take over as Chief Justice from Justice Sanjeev Kumar who has been serving as Acting Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since June 2, 2026. Justice Bhati was a lawyer practicing across several areas of law for nearly 25 before he was elevated to the Bench of the Rajasthan High Court on November 16, 2016. As a lawyer, he served as a Additional Advocate General for the State and was elected as President of the High Court Lawyers Association at different points Justice Bhati's wife, Justice Nupur Bhati was also elevated as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

items.title: Exclusive: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice Sanjay K Agrawal as Rajasthan High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Sanjay K Agrawal of the Chhattisgarh High Court as the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, Bar & Bench has exclusively learnt. Justice Agrawal is presently a judge of the Chhattisgarh High Court. He was elevated as an Additional Judge of that Court in September 2013 and made a permanent judge in March 2016. Before his elevation, he had served as the Advocate General of Chhattisgarh. Significantly, the Collegium has also proposed that Justice Agrawal be immediately transferred to the Rajasthan High Court, pending his appointment as its Chief Justice. The move would mean that even if the process for his appointment as Chief Justice takes time, Justice Agrawal would join the Rajasthan High Court as its senior-most judge. The development assumes significance in the backdrop of the controversy surrounding the present Acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma. Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta recently wrote to CJI Surya Kant seeking Justice Sharma's transfer out of Rajasthan and appointment of a regular Chief Justice from another High Court. items.title: Maharashtra family court judges cannot be treated as judicial officers for High Court elevation: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to revisit its ruling which had held that judges belonging to Maharashtra's separate family court cadre cannot be treated as holding a "judicial office" for determining eligibility for appointment as High Court judges under Article 217 of the Constitution. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea by seven family court judges seeking a declaration that presiding officers of family courts be treated as holding judicial office for the purposes of elevation to the High Court. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Senior Advocate R Basant , appearing for the petitioners, urged the Court to reconsider its 2010 ruling in ST Joshi v. High Court of Judicature at Bombay . He argued that circumstances had materially changed since, with Maharashtra having appointed only judicial officers or advocates as family court judges for the past 36 years. items.title: AI-generated work can get copyright but AI system cannot be author: Indian copyright office
items.summary: An artificial intelligence (AI) system cannot be recognised as an author under the Copyright Act, 1957, the Copyright Office has ruled while rejecting an application that named the AI system DABUS as the author of an artwork. However, Registrar of Copyrights Dr. Unnat P Pandit clarified that a work generated through AI or computational processes satisfies the originality requirement under copyright law. The ruling came on an application filed by American computer scientist Stephen L Thaler for registration of copyright in an artwork titled A Recent Entrance to Paradise . The application identified the Device for the Autonomous Bootstrapping of Unified Sentience (DABUS) as the author and Thaler as the copyright owner. The Copyright Office concluded that Thaler, rather than DABUS, was the person who caused the artwork to be created within the meaning of Section 2(d)(vi) of the Act. “DABUS is not a natural or juristic person recognised in law and cannot be entered as author under Section 2(d)(vi) ,” the Registrar held.
